title: A Golf Ball Hit on the Moon Flew 40 Yards, Not Miles
hook: In 1971, Alan Shepard hit two golf balls on the Moon

open.title: An astronaut swore his moon golf shot went for miles, until his film was checked 50 years later
open.line: In 1971 an astronaut hit golf balls on the Moon. He said one flew miles and miles. 50 years later, someone went back over the film. What did it show?

summary: Apollo 14's Shepard hit two golf balls on the Moon and said they flew for miles. A 2021 analysis put them at about 24 yards and 40 yards.

text: On February 6, 1971, Apollo 14 commander Alan Shepard swung a golf club on the Moon.
The club was a 6-iron head attached to the handle of a tool for scooping up moon rocks.
He had smuggled the head aboard in a sock.
His spacesuit was stiff, so he swung with one hand.
The first ball was a mishit and landed in a nearby crater.
After hitting the second ball, he shouted,

panels.text: With weak gravity, it must have gone really far, right?

text: In 2021, imaging specialist Andy Saunders matched the old film with photos from a lunar orbiter and found where the balls landed.
The first ball flew about 24 yards, and the second about 40 yards.
